sections.title: Open-weight AI models
sections.text: Ollama runs so-called “open” models: their weights are published, and they can be installed on your own server. I choose the model for the task, the language and the hardware, after tests on your documents. A few model families:

defs.text: Several sizes, good in many languages, including Asian languages. Some versions can also read images.
Compact, multilingual models that run on modest hardware. Some versions can also read images.
Very widely used, with a large community. Its licence sets conditions of use.
A French company; efficient models, comfortable in French and English.
Including models that “reason” step by step before answering: useful for analysis, but slower.
OpenAI's open models, released under the Apache 2.0 licence.
They find the right passage in your documents: the basis of an assistant that answers from your own texts.
More powerful, but your data goes through their provider's servers. Useful when confidentiality allows it.

sections.title: Why local AI
list: You stay in control of your data: it stays on your server.
Less dependence on an outside service, its prices and its terms.
It can work on a private network, with no internet access.
The model and its settings are chosen for your task.

sections.title: The hardware

sections.title: How I do it
list: We start small, with a single task.
You stay in control: the AI suggests, a person decides.

sections.title: Good to know

The server needs an air-conditioned room and a UPS.
Keeping AI on your premises limits how far your data travels, but security also depends on the server: updates, access, backups.
Models change quickly: new versions come out every few months. Each model has its own licence, to be checked for your use.

sections.title: GLPI, IT asset management
sections.text: GLPI is open-source IT asset management software. It brings together in one place everything the business owns:
list: The inventory of computers, servers, printers and network equipment.
Hardware: specifications, location, user, warranty.
Installed software and licenses.
The history of each device.
Support requests and interventions, tracked until they are resolved.

sections.title: GLPI Agent, automatic inventory
sections.text: GLPI Agent is a small program installed on each computer and each server, running Windows, Linux or macOS. It regularly sends the machine's inventory to GLPI, with no manual entry. So you know:
list: which computers are in your IT estate;
which operating system each one runs, and which version;
which software is installed, and in which versions;
which devices are tracked;
how your IT estate changes: machines added or removed, software updated.

sections.title: Security watch
sections.text: The inventory tells you what is installed. The security watch tells you what is a problem. I follow the security information published for the software in your inventory:
list: outdated versions;
software at end of support, which no longer receives patches;
security advisories from software publishers;
published vulnerabilities (CVE references);
available patches;
priorities: what to update first.

sections.title: Monitoring: Zabbix and Grafana
sections.text: Security also means seeing a problem coming in time. Two free tools work together:

defs.text: Continuously monitors servers, virtual machines, the network and services, and sends an alert when something is wrong: a service stopped, a disk nearly full, an unusual load.
Reads the data from Zabbix and shows it in clear dashboards: the state of your IT assets, the current alerts and their history, on a single screen.

sections.title: What GLPI Agent does not do
sections.text: GLPI Agent is not a vulnerability scanner: it lists what is installed, nothing more. Matching that list against published flaws is separate work, a security watch, based on the inventory. It is the combination of the two that makes it possible to act.

sections.title: Day-to-day security
list: System hardening: unnecessary services turned off, security settings applied.
Update management: tested, then deployed.
Accounts and permissions: everyone has access only to what they need.
Access control, including remote access.
Backups, with a copy in a second location and restore tests.
Service monitoring with Zabbix, dashboards with Grafana.
Logs: keeping track of what happens on the servers.
Incident tracking in GLPI.
Documentation of your IT estate: what exists, where, and how it is set up.

sections.title: What I don't do
list: I do not carry out certified audits or penetration tests.
I do not issue compliance certifications.
My work is day-to-day security: IT assets that are known, up to date, backed up and monitored.

sections.title: Let's talk about your situation
sections.text: Every business is different. Tell me what worries you, and we'll work out together what is useful for you.

sections.title: Why Odoo 19 Community
list: It is the open-source edition of Odoo (LGPL v3 licence): no per-user subscription to pay to the publisher.

Your data sits in a database you control.

Odoo 20 is already out, but the open-source OCA modules that complement the free edition are mostly available for version 19: as of November 2026, very few have been adapted to version 20. When they are, I will tell you whether switching is worth it.

sections.text: Some apps are only in the paid edition, Odoo Enterprise. Full accounting, for example: Community has invoicing (invoices and payments), and open-source modules from the OCA community (Odoo Community Association) add accounting features, depending on their availability for version 19. Odoo Studio, the tool for changing Odoo without programming, is also Enterprise-only: with Community, those changes are made with custom modules. If one day you need Enterprise, you can switch editions.

sections.title: Adapted to the Cambodian market
sections.text: Odoo lists Khmer among its languages, but the publisher's translation is almost empty: in Odoo 19, fewer than one text in ten is translated into Khmer in the Sales, Accounting, Inventory and Point of Sale apps. sections.title: Which edition to choose
sections.text: Mattermost comes in several editions, and the differences matter. I explain them to you before you choose:

defs.text: Free (MIT licence). The core of the messaging, with the full message history, but fewer features than the other editions. Intended for small teams that do not need single sign-on (SSO).

Free, under a commercial licence, for teams of fewer than 50 people. It has the features of the paid editions, but only the last 10,000 messages, across all channels, stay visible and searchable. The publisher announces other limits, such as 40-minute calls.

Paid, by subscription. Professional adds, among other things, connection to the company directory (AD/LDAP), single sign-on (SSO), guest accounts, multi-factor authentication, group calls and screen sharing. Enterprise adds compliance archiving and high availability.

sections.title: Mattermost or Nextcloud Talk?
sections.text: Nextcloud also has its own messaging, Talk. If you install Nextcloud for your files, Talk is often enough. Mattermost is designed first for team discussion: many channels, threads, links with your other tools.

inventoryFlow.title: How it works, in five steps

steps.title: GLPI Agent collects
steps.text: On each workstation and each server, the agent records the hardware, the operating system and the installed software.

steps.title: GLPI centralizes
steps.text: The inventories arrive in GLPI: an overview of your IT assets, kept up to date.

steps.title: Versions are analyzed
steps.text: Software and versions are grouped together: what is outdated or at end of support stands out.

steps.title: The security watch connects them
steps.text: These versions are compared with published security advisories and vulnerabilities.

steps.title: Priorities are set
steps.text: Software that needs particular attention is identified, and updates are done in the right order.

inventoryFlow.note: GLPI Agent takes the inventory. Detecting vulnerabilities is a separate step: the security watch, done from that inventory.

hms.text: Bookings, front desk, billing, housekeeping, restaurant, vehicle rental and reports. In five languages, on computer, tablet or phone.

learnkh.title: Learn-kh
learnkh.text: Learn Khmer, French and English, starting from French, English or Khmer. 60 lessons, the alphabet with audio, a glossary of about 600 words and flashcards.

acpc.title: Acpc
acpc.text: The Amstrad CPC 464, 664 and 6128, the 6128 Plus and the GX4000 console on an Android phone or tablet. Discs, tapes and cartridges, automatic game start, save states. About 700 titles tested.

asokoban.title: ASokoban
asokoban.text: The crate-pushing puzzle: 70 hand-designed levels, every one verified solvable, on a 2D board or an animated 3D one. In English and Khmer.

snake3d.title: 3D Snake
snake3d.text: Snake in 3D, seen from behind the head, on islands with hills, terraces and ramps. 14 stages, 9 sanctuaries, 18 languages including Khmer. Models, textures, sounds and music are generated by code.

velocity.title: Velocity
velocity.text: Eight teams of hovering ships on twelve circuits, from a megacity at dusk to a colony on Mars. Six game modes, a career, championships, eight weapons and power-ups.

rally.title: Cambodia Rally
rally.text: A 3D race on the real roads around the temples of Angkor. 2 to 8 players, one phone each, on the same Wi-Fi or a hotspot, no internet needed. 8 vehicles, 2 tracks, 7 languages.
rally.shows: Shows: 3D mobile game, local multiplayer, translation into 7 languages.

angkor.title: Angkor World Engine
angkor.text: The Angkor and Siem Reap area rebuilt in 3D at real scale, about 37 × 45 km, from open map data. You can fly over it or drive through it.
angkor.shows: Shows: map data processing, 3D, performance on phones.

synth.title: Synth Rack
synth.text: 26 synthesizers and drum machines inspired by vintage models, playable in the browser, with a MIDI sequencer.
synth.shows: Shows: audio and web, nothing to install.

vsm.title: VSM Studio
vsm.text: A music studio with 64 simulated instruments, a sequencer, audio recording, a mixing desk and plugin support.
vsm.shows: Shows: demanding desktop software, audio processing.

about.title: About
about.lead: I'm Stefan, founder of Chantrea Systems, based in Kampot, Cambodia.

sections.title: Why "Chantrea"
sections.text: Chantrea means "moonlight" in Khmer. A calm light that illuminates without dazzling. That is what I want to bring to your tools.

sections.title: Clear communication
sections.text: Write in your language: I answer with the help of AI translation. Nothing lost between departments. I tell you clearly what I can do, and what I don't do.

sections.title: My role
sections.text: I am responsible for every project, from the first conversation to technical follow-up: design, development, installation, commissioning and maintenance. You always know who is looking after your setup.

sections.title: What Chantrea Systems does
list: Software and digital solutions: business software, web and Android apps, multilingual websites.
AI and automation: AI models added to your tools, installed on your premises if you wish.
Infrastructure and systems: Windows and Linux servers, virtualization, monitoring, backups.
Cybersecurity and IT asset management: inventory, tracking of security flaws, updates, access.

sections.title: Where I work
sections.text: Based in Kampot, I work on site in the region and anywhere in Cambodia. Depending on the project, I can also travel abroad, anywhere in the world. For clients abroad, the work can also be done remotely.

sections.title: What interests me
sections.text: Linux and free software, virtualization and server administration, Android, artificial intelligence tools, video games, creative coding.

sections.text: Chantrea Systems is looking for a certified translator, English or French ↔ Khmer.

jobs.title: Jobs
jobs.lead: Chantrea Systems is looking for a certified translator, English or French ↔ Khmer, to work with Stefan with Cambodian businesses.

sections.title: The role
list: Be the link in Khmer between clients and Stefan: meetings, messages, explanations about the projects.
Translate and proofread the Khmer texts of software (Odoo, HMS), documents and invoices. AI often prepares a first draft: you correct and approve it.
Follow the same clients as far as possible, so they keep the same contact person.

sections.title: The profile
list: Khmer native speaker, fluent in English or French.
Translator certified by the Cambodian authorities.
Knowledge of Cambodian taxation: VAT, invoices, tax returns, accounting vocabulary.
Comfortable with computers. IT knowledge is a plus, not a requirement.

sections.title: Conditions
list: Location: Kampot or remote.
Type of collaboration: freelance, paid per project.

sections.title: How to apply
sections.text: Send by email a CV, a copy of your certification and a few lines about your experience, in Khmer and in English or French.
